task.description: Hard gate: verify every REQ-172 acceptance criterion has a runnable, non-skipped test, that the shared parity harness is genuinely exercised against BOTH executors (not just structurally present), that fixtures are self-sufficient and isolated, and that the mutation-testing claims are real -- independently re-apply at least the most consequential mutant yourself (e.g. the fail-uninterceptability mechanism, or the write-discard-on-failure-arm mechanism) and confirm the suite catches it, per this project's standard discipline of not merely trusting TEST-DESIGNER's own mutation report. Confirm the :wasm_hang-tagged test integrates correctly with the existing test_helper.exs exclusion/isolated-subprocess convention (ISS-0352) rather than reintroducing that CI hazard.
acceptance_criteria: ONE shared scenario definition is executed against BOTH the Lua executor and the WASM handler, asserting identical observable outcomes -- WASM-12's own acceptance criterion -- rather than two separately written suites; the shared harness is a single named module or fixture, quoted in the moduledoc

a test asserts a guest that writes variables and then FAILS leaves instance variable state unchanged, asserted separately for each failure arm: a guest trap, fuel exhaustion (REQ-169), memory cap (REQ-169), wall-clock timeout (REQ-170), and fail
a test asserts a guest that writes several variables and succeeds applies all of them with no observable partial state

a test asserts call_service returns a structured error to the guest on service failure rather than trapping, and a separate test asserts a missing service capability fails per REQ-167 -- the two behaviours asserted distinctly
a test asserts a guest that attempts to catch or ignore its own fail STILL yields a failed outcome and does not run to completion -- the WASM analogue of REQ-161's uninterceptable-termination test

any semantic difference between the Lua and WASM host APIs that is not purely ABI (string encoding, return shape) is enumerated explicitly in the moduledoc with its justification; the moduledoc states that WASM-12 limits differences to ABI, so an unlisted one means the requirement is unmet

the moduledoc states that the Lua host API is the definition WASM conforms to per decision 0014 Decision (4), and that no Lua-side behaviour was changed to ease parity; confirmed by `git diff --stat` scoped to this requirement's commits showing no Lua host-API implementation file modified
mix test and mix compile --warnings-as-errors both pass with real output quoted

result.summary: Hard gate PASSED. All 8 acceptance criteria independently re-derived (not taken on TEST-DESIGNER's report). Independently re-applied the do_fail/5 fail-uninterceptability mutant (removed the stash_fail_signal/2 call) myself in-tree -- caught decisively (7 of the file's tests failed, plus mix compile --warnings-as-errors itself failed on the resulting unused-function warning, an incidental second signal). Reverted via `git checkout --`, confirmed byte-identical (md5sum 37152b8d723248b646ec8cf39ff67078 before and after) and `git status --porcelain lib/ test/` empty, then re-ran the file green (33 passed, 1 excluded). Ran full `mix test` via scripts/test_parallel.sh (2429 tests, 2430/2434 passed, 4 failures) -- all 4 failures structurally cleared as pre-existing/environmental (none of their files or dependency modules appear in `git diff --name-only main...HEAD`; the two rust-pin toolchain tests fail with ErlangError :enoent because `rustc` is absent from this sandbox's PATH, confirmed directly). Targeted test/letflow/engine/wasm/ + test/letflow/engine/lua/ run: 385 passed, 7 excluded, zero failures -- matches handoff's claimed count exactly, independently reproduced. Also ran the isolated `mix test --only wasm_hang` subprocess directly (the ISS-0352 convention `mix letflow.check.test` automates): 7 passed, 0 failures, confirming the new :wasm_hang-tagged test (req172_write_then_hang.wat) integrates correctly rather than reintroducing the cascading-timeout hazard. mix compile --warnings-as-errors: clean, exit 0.
